files.prompt: A three story garden style apartment complex in an invented California foothill community, two long buildings with warm cream stucco walls, dark grey metal roofs, white window trim and small balconies, seen at eye level from across a landscaped courtyard in late afternoon golden light, dry golden grass hills behind. The grounds show careful wildfire defensible space: a clean strip of grey gravel along every wall, no plants, mulch or wood touching the buildings, low green succulents and widely spaced trees with their lower branches trimmed high, a short mowed green lawn, metal railings on the balconies, a low metal fence. Calm, well kept, wide establishing composition with open sky above the roofs. Photorealistic, natural colours, no people, no cars, no text, no signs, no logos, no fire, no smoke, no flames.
Same call as round3/synthetic-apartments-1.png.

Photorealistic late afternoon photo of an invented large single story California ranch home, about 2,800 square feet, on a wooded lot in dry foothills. An L shaped plan: a long main wing with four bedroom windows along the front, and a projecting wing with an attached two car garage with a plain dark bronze metal sectional garage door, a covered front entry porch with fieldstone columns where the two wings meet, and a fieldstone chimney. Seen from across the front yard at a three quarter angle so the front of both wings and one gable end are in view, camera about 90 feet away at a height of 6 feet, 28 mm lens. The whole house sits in the middle third of the picture with open sky and treetops above it and dry yard in front. Every wall is the same warm earth tone stucco over a low stacked fieldstone base; no wood siding anywhere. Low pitched brown concrete tile roof with hips and gables, dry pine needles drifted in the roof valleys, and one long ponderosa pine branch hanging over the garage roof. Dark bronze metal gutters overflowing with needles and leaves. Open eaves with the wooden rafter tails exposed along every wall, and a large square gable vent with coarse open mesh in the gable end. Against the gable end wall: a tall stack of split firewood leaning on the stucco, and a weathered wood fence with a gate that runs right into the corner of the wall. Along the base of the walls: drifts of dry oak leaves, bark mulch, dense junipers touching the house under the windows, dry tall grass. Tall ponderosa pines and oaks behind and around the house. Low golden sun from the left just above the tree line, warm side light raking across the stucco, long soft shadows, light haze in the air, a clear pale sky. No people, no text, no signs, no logos, no house numbers, no vehicles, no fire, no smoke.

The same photo, same house, same camera position and framing, same light, pixel for pixel. Change only the roof and gutters: the dry pine needles are gone from the roof valleys and the roof tiles are clean, the dark bronze gutters are clean and fitted with metal gutter guards, and the long pine branch over the garage roof is cut back so the nearest branch is at least ten feet from the roof. Everything else stays exactly as it is, including the open eaves and rafter tails, the gable vent, the firewood, the fence and gate, the leaves, the junipers, the grass, the trees behind the house and the sky.

The same photo, same house, same camera position and framing, same light, pixel for pixel. Change only two things. First, the eaves: the exposed wooden rafter tails under the roof edge are gone, boxed in with smooth flat soffits finished in the same earth tone stucco as the walls, along every wall and under the porch gable. Second, the gable vent: the coarse open wooden grid in the gable is removed and replaced, in the same opening, by a flat dark bronze metal vent panel covered with very fine metal mesh, so fine that no openings can be seen and it reads as a smooth dark screen. Everything else stays exactly as it is: the roof tiles stay clean with no pine needles, the gutters keep their metal gutter guards, the pine branch stays cut back, and the firewood, fence and gate, leaves, junipers, grass, trees and sky do not change.

The same photo, same house, same camera position and framing, same light, pixel for pixel. Change only what touches the walls. First, the tall stack of split firewood leaning on the gable end wall is gone completely; the stucco wall and fieldstone base behind it are bare and clean. Second, the weathered wood fence and gate no longer touch the house: the last section of fence next to the wall corner is replaced by a plain dark metal panel, and the wood fence now ends about five feet away from the wall. The stucco walls themselves stay the same. Everything else stays exactly as it is: the clean roof, the gutters with their guards, the boxed eaves, the fine mesh gable vent, the cut back pine branch, and the dry leaves, bark mulch, junipers and dry grass along the base of the walls do not change.

The same photo, same house, same camera position and framing, same light, pixel for pixel. Change only the ground within five feet of the walls. The pile of dry leaves, the bark mulch and the dry grass at the base of the walls are gone, and the junipers growing against the front wall under the windows are removed. In their place, a five foot wide band of plain gray gravel runs along the base of every wall, from the garage and porch along the long front wall to the gable end wall and the metal panel, with three low succulents spaced far apart in it. Beyond the gravel band the grass is green and mowed short. Everything else stays exactly as it is: the clean roof, the gutters with their guards, the boxed eaves, the fine mesh gable vent, the cut back pine branch, the bare gable end wall with no firewood, the dark metal panel and the wood gate, the driveway, the trees and the sky.

Photorealistic wide view from a high rocky ridge over a wooded valley at late afternoon. In the foreground, close to the lens, the ridge line with dry grass, granite and a few manzanita shrubs. Below, a valley of ponderosa pines and oaks with layered haze. In a clearing a little below the middle of the frame, far below and small, the exact same L shaped single story house as in both references, seen from the same side as the references so its front faces the camera: the attached garage wing at the left with its dark bronze garage door facing front and the fieldstone chimney at the far left end of that wing, the covered entry porch with fieldstone columns where the two wings meet, and the long bedroom wing running to the right ending in the gable end with its large square vent, the firewood and the wood fence and gate on that gable end wall. Earth tone stucco walls, fieldstone base, brown tile roof. The house plan, the order of its parts from left to right and the side facing the camera must match the references exactly; no wing projects toward the camera. The camera looks down the valley along the same line as the second reference, so a straight glide down over the pines would arrive at that view. The sun sits low just above the far ridge at the left, a small bright sunstar breaking through the tops of the pines, golden backlight rimming the trees. A thin layer of distant gray haze lies along the far hills and softens the light; warm amber tones, long shadows. No flames, no fire, no smoke columns, no burning trees, no glowing embers. No people, no text, no logos, no vehicles.

files.prompt: One continuous, unbroken shot with no cuts. A very slow, perfectly steady descent at constant speed from above the pines down to the base of the house's front wall near the gable end corner. The camera sinks past pine branches and cones that drift close by the lens with strong parallax, crosses the yard and settles low, about three feet off the ground, looking along the front wall at the pile of dry oak leaves against the fieldstone base, with the stacked firewood at the corner. The house, its earth tone stucco, fieldstone base, open eaves with rafter tails, bronze gutters and tile roof stay exactly the same throughout. Warm late afternoon golden light, thin haze, long soft shadows. Photorealistic, cinema camera, 35 mm, shallow depth of field at the end. Nothing changes except the camera and a light breeze in the branches. No flames, no fire, no people, no text, no logos. The camera never stops, never turns sharply and never changes speed.
